summary:
The Remote Anti-Climate Issues Tool (FRAPC), developed by the Cosmos Program, is an intuitive, superintelligent tool designed to predict imminent climate tragedies in peripheral neighborhoods of Manaus. The solution uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data to detect ground deformations and monitor soil instability caused by rainfall. This information is processed and translated into alerts, which are broadcast to the population through an accessible interface implemented on physical totems.

The importance of this initiative lies in the direct protection of these areas, where landslides have a deeply negative impact on local communities. By leveraging advanced orbital data to forecast disasters, the project democratizes access to risk information. Installing the totems in strategic locations ensures that residents receive early, easy-to-understand warnings, providing the necessary reaction time to evacuate danger zones, save lives, and prevent major tragedies during the rainy season.
details:
The Remote Anti-Climate Issues Tool (FRAPC), developed by the Cosmos Program team as part of NASA Space Apps Manaus 2026, is an intuitive, artificial intelligence-based solution created to predict imminent climate tragedies, focusing on landslides in the peripheral neighborhoods of Manaus. The system operates by collecting and analyzing Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data extracted from the NASA Earthdata and ASF Vertex platforms, specifically selected to monitor the Amazon region and detect micro-deformations and soil instabilities caused by rainfall accumulation. This information is processed by predictive algorithms and translated into clear, intuitive alerts, broadcast to the population through an accessible interface implemented on physical totems installed at strategic points within the communities. Among the main benefits of the solution are the democratization of access to highly complex orbital data and the issuance of early warnings, guaranteeing residents the necessary reaction time to evacuate danger zones, reduce property damage, and save lives during the region's intense rainy season.

For the technical development of the project, the team used Python in the VS Code environment, employing the Pandas library to process and structure geospatial datasets and the LightGBM framework to train the artificial intelligence model, while the interactive and accessible interface for the totems was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The scientific foundation regarding climate issues and disaster dynamics in Manaus was grounded in research from the SciELO platform, complemented by the use of Canva to create FRAPC’s visual identity and logo, as well as Adobe Premiere to edit the presentation video. The creative aspect of the project lies precisely in bridging cutting-edge orbital remote sensing with community social inclusion, bringing critical information directly to the streets through easy-to-read physical totems that eliminate the need for residents to own smartphones or individual data plans. During the planning phase, the team incorporated data from the 2022 IBGE Census and analyzed essential factors for the project, such as the socioeconomic vulnerability of peripheral areas, the severity of Amazonian rainfall, and communication accessibility for diverse audiences. This stage also defined a practical execution timeline, divided between mockup development, totem manufacturing, and the continuous implementation of improvements.
